body:
Raised 2026-10-03 (America/Los_Angeles), explicitly requested by the user. Engineering performance only; no geographic or historical research/imports.

Problem and UI: src/main.js initially displays "Preparing your atlas…" in #loading. start() awaits loadGeography(), builds geometry/maps, then awaits loadYear(), which changes the message to "Loading [year]…". Initial usable-map time includes both stages; do not time just the first message or hide it early to claim a speedup. User reports slow initial loading. Retained Site23 measurements from PR #630 show 34.713–36.325 seconds for fresh browser initialization, distinct from subsequent year switching. These are cloud Chromium/private GET-proxy measurements, not fresh measurements of the current release or real phones. Provider idle/wake state was not established.

Existing evidence: data/engineering/year-switch-final-20261003-7e91/README.md and site23-evidence-transfer.json retain exact traces/receipts. Prior startup observations: geography 54 requests/~9.49 MB, ownership 56 requests/~47.61 MB, reference attributes 72 requests/~2.15 MB, browser task CPU ~5.34–5.51 seconds. Overlapping request groups cannot be summed as elapsed critical path. Reuse evidence rather than restart from guesses.

Bounded scope (at most three focused PRs):
1. Reproduce current-release fresh-cache and repeat-visit startup end to end. Separate release/bootstrap reads, geometry and identity loading, ownership transfer/decompression/assembly/GPU upload, reference attributes, initial dated snapshot, client resolution and first visible interactive render. Preserve actual critical-path timings, request counts/bytes, memory observations and every sample; identify what genuinely blocks first use.
2. Implement the largest measured startup-only improvements, such as revision/hash-safe cache reuse, eliminating duplicate or unnecessary startup requests, avoiding serial waits, or deferring nonessential inspector/search/evidence payloads until needed. Only defer data if normal map fills, borders, picking and selected-year correctness are already supported by complete validated inputs. Do not weaken integrity or assert unsupported values. No renderer rewrite, arbitrary grid coarsening or geographic aggregation without a separately reviewed task.
3. Independently review, coordinate publication and verify the exact deployed result with before/after browser traces and rollback receipts. Aim for first correct interactive map within 10 seconds under documented comparable baseline conditions; report a missed target honestly rather than closing on local tests or loader-message changes. Retain repeat-visit and representative selected-year checks.

Correctness and acceptance:
- Start timing at navigation; finish only when the selected-year map is correct and interactive, with loading state cleared. Expose actual failures/retry; no success on partial or mixed-release map.
- Preserve full whole-location modes, complete hierarchy, stable IDs, original history/source/archive bytes, withdrawal authority, temporal intervals and consistent release/revision pins.
- Fixed ownership assets may initialize at startup but must be reused during zoom/pan/resize/year switches. Benchmark zero extra navigation ownership recompilations/uploads and preserve current selection/latest-wins behavior.
- Verify cache invalidation on release changes, integrity/missing-asset errors, GPU/fallback behavior, loading UX and all existing map-mode/inspector contracts. No new physical-device certificate is required; actual-phone task #49 was explicitly deprioritized.
- Keep current Site package/asset and memory limits; no emergency source deletion. If measured improvement requires larger asset-hosting changes, coordinate #54/#55 rather than duplicate them.
- Production verification needs authorized private Site access and the designated publisher. Inspect access early, document genuine blockers, never paste/rotate credentials or deploy competing versions. Source tests alone do not establish production speed.

Coordination and readiness: Ready for one engineering worker's serialized claim, no geography dependency. #638 owns subsequent populated-year navigation; #22 tracks that goal. This issue owns initial startup. #54 owns external immutable-asset delivery/access/manifest tooling; #55 its publication proof. Inspect their claims/current PRs before touching shared src/data-client.js or ownership loader modules; record an explicit interface/file agreement if both are active. Coordinate release publication with #6/#51 and the designated publisher. No active PR found specifically implementing startup latency at creation; recheck at claim time. Separate independently owned PRs; never claim other issues or overwrite their evidence.

Use current docs/prompts/ENGINEERING.txt, docs/WORKER_COORDINATION.md and docs/PREMERGE_EVIDENCE_REVIEW.md. Retain baseline and final whole-file evidence in the owned job directory, versioned hashes/pins, honest validation limits and distinct exact-head implementation review. Live release checks also need appropriate release/source review. Use exactly one Refs/Closes reference to this issue per PR. Completion is measured deployed acceptance, not the number of merged PRs.
